title: Attention, Zoo Visitors
text:
Ding, dong! Attention, all zoo visitors. This is an important announcement from the front office.

The lion show will start in {number} minutes. Today Leo the Lion will jump through a hoop and {verb} on a big {adjective} ball. Please clap {adverb} so he knows you are watching. We have also found a lost item near the penguin pool. It is a small {noun} with a sticker on it. If it belongs to you, please come to the front gate.

A reminder that the gorillas are having their afternoon nap. Please do not {verb} near their window. The last time someone did, the baby gorilla {past tense verb} for an hour.

Today's special at the snack stand is a {food} sandwich with a side of {plural noun}. Thank you, and enjoy your {adjective} day at the zoo!

title: My Zoo Field Trip Report
text:
Last Friday, my class went to the zoo on a big yellow bus. Our teacher, Mr. Ruiz, made us hold hands and walk {adverb}.

First we saw the giraffes. They are very tall and have long {plural noun}. One giraffe tried to nibble my friend Leo's {noun}, but Mr. Ruiz said it was just being friendly. Next we visited the reptile house. There was a turtle {verb ending in ing} in a tiny pool. I learned that turtles can live to be {number} years old.

My favorite animal was the zebra. Its stripes are black and white and a little bit {color}. It {past tense verb} at me, so I waved back. For lunch we ate sandwiches by the duck pond. A duck took my {food} and ran away.

In conclusion, the zoo is {adjective}, and I would like to {verb} there every day. The end.

title: Penguin House Rules
text:
Welcome to the Penguin House! It is very cold in here, so please zip up your coat. Then read these rules.

Rule one: Do not tap on the glass. The penguins do not like it, and they will {verb} at you. Rule two: Lunch is at noon. Today the zookeeper will give the penguins ice cubes and {number} {plural noun}. Rule three: Please walk {adverb}. The floor is very slippery, and so are the penguins.

Rule four: Our oldest penguin, Mr. Waddles, likes to wear a tiny {adjective} bow tie. Please tell him he looks nice. Rule five: If a penguin starts {verb ending in ing}, it means she wants to play. You may wave your {body part} at her.

Rule six: No {plural noun} are allowed in the Penguin House. Last week a boy brought some, and the penguins {past tense verb} for three days. Thank you for visiting, and please waddle {adverb} on your way out!

title: Wanted: Zookeeper Helper
text:
The Sunnyside Zoo is looking for a helper! Do you love animals? Are you {adjective} and good at sharing? Then this job is for you.

Every morning, you will help the zookeeper brush the elephants' {plural noun}. Then you will sing a song to the koalas so they can {verb}. On Tuesdays, you will read a book about {plural noun} to the owls.

You will also help clean the hippo pool. This is a messy job, so please wear a raincoat and a {noun} on your head. The hippos like to splash {adverb} when someone new is {verb ending in ing}.

You will be paid with a big smile and {number} free {plural noun} every Friday. Our last helper {past tense verb} so much that the monkeys gave her a medal. To apply, draw a picture of your favorite {animal} and bring it to the front gate.

title: Your Guide to the Zoo Map
text:
Welcome to Pine Hill Zoo! Here is a quick guide to help you find your way.

Start at the front gate and walk past the big fountain. The fountain was a gift from a very {adjective} hippo named Gloria. If you toss a {noun} in, Gloria will {verb} for you. Turn left at the Monkey House. You will hear the monkeys {verb ending in ing} before you see them. They are practicing for their play, which is all about {plural noun}.

Keep walking until you reach the giant tortoise. He moves {adverb}, so he may still be in the same spot as this morning. Say hello! His name is {name}. Next you will find the Bird Garden and the snack stand. The snack stand sells popcorn, juice, and {food}.

Our map ends at the gift shop. There you can buy a stuffed panda, a zoo hat, or {number} {plural noun}. Have a {adjective} visit!

title: Zoo News: The Elephant Learns to Paint
text:
Good morning! This is Zoo News, and we have a {adjective} story for you today.

Penny the Elephant has become an artist. Every morning, she holds a paintbrush with her trunk and paints pictures of {plural noun}. Her favorite color to use is {color}. "We first noticed when she {past tense verb} on the wall of her barn," said zookeeper Mr. Tran. "So we gave her real paper. Now she paints {adverb} for hours."

Penny's paintings are now hanging in the Zoo Cafe. Her most famous one shows a giraffe holding a {noun}. People line up to {verb} in front of it.

Next week, Penny will start teaching an art class for the monkeys. So far the monkeys are mostly {verb ending in ing}. Penny says they are doing a {adjective} job. That is all for Zoo News. Stay {adjective}, zoo fans!

title: A Day in the Life of a Zookeeper
text:
6:00 in the morning: My alarm went off. I put on my zoo shirt and my lucky {adjective} boots.
7:00: Breakfast time for the animals! The giraffes got leaves, the bears got berries, and the parrots got {plural noun}.

9:00: The baby elephant would not get out of the pool. I asked her nicely to {verb}, but she {past tense verb} and splashed me instead.
12:00: Lunch! I ate my sandwich with the penguins. One of them always tries to take my {noun}.

3:00: The kangaroos had a hopping contest. The winner hopped {number} times in a row and won a {adjective} ribbon.
5:00: I checked on everyone before I went home. The lions were {verb ending in ing}, the monkeys were telling jokes, and the sloth was still eating breakfast.

8:00 at night: I fell asleep {adverb} and dreamed about {plural noun}.

title: Lunch for the Hungry Hippo
text:
Hector the Hippo is always hungry. Here is how the zookeepers make his favorite lunch.

You will need one giant watermelon, a wheelbarrow full of lettuce, and {number} {plural noun}. You will also need a very {adjective} spoon. First, cut the watermelon into slices as big as a {noun}. Hector likes them big. Next, mix the lettuce with a scoop of {food}. Stir it {adverb} until it looks like a salad. Then add a handful of {plural noun}.

Now it is time for the best part. Carry the lunch to the pool and call, "Hector, it is time to {verb}!" He will swim over {verb ending in ing} with joy.

Last Tuesday, when Hector finished his lunch, he {past tense verb} and fell asleep in the sun. Hippos are very {adjective} eaters.

title: Meet the Zoo's Oldest Tortoise
text:
This week, the Zoo Kids Club talked with Grandpa Shell, the oldest tortoise at our zoo. He is {number} years old.

Kids Club: What was the zoo like when you were young?
Grandpa Shell: It was very {adjective}. Back then, the monkeys wore hats and the giraffes played {plural noun} every afternoon.
Kids Club: What is your secret to staying so happy?
Grandpa Shell: Eat your greens, take lots of naps, and never {verb} after dinner. Also, I keep a {noun} under my shell for good luck.

Kids Club: Who is your best friend?
Grandpa Shell: A flamingo named Rosie. Every morning, we go {verb ending in ing} together. She is much faster than me, but she waits {adverb}.
Kids Club: What do you do on your birthday?
Grandpa Shell: The zookeepers bring me a cake made of {food}. Last year I {past tense verb} so hard that my shell wiggled.

Kids Club: Thank you, Grandpa Shell!
Grandpa Shell: You are welcome. Now please let me get back to {verb ending in ing}.

title: A Thank-You Note from the Panda
text:
Dear Visitors,

My name is Bao, and I am the panda who lives next to the gift shop. I am writing to say thank you for visiting me this summer.

Thank you to the girl who waved at me with her {body part}. It made me feel very {adjective}. Thank you also to the boy who sang me a song about {plural noun}. I liked it so much that I {past tense verb} all afternoon.

I know some of you wanted to see me {verb ending in ing}, but I was usually asleep. Pandas sleep a lot. Next time, I will try to {verb} for you. My favorite snack is still bamboo, but this summer I also tried a {noun}. It was {adjective}.

Please come back soon. I will be here, sitting {adverb} on my favorite rock and dreaming about {food}.

Your friend,
Bao
